p.n: The Cat and the Rat Escape
The Cat Calls Back the Rat

body.p:
The rat came out after that, saw the cat
and dreaded coming close to him. ‘Come, friend,’ cried the cat, ‘you who have done a good deed.

p.n: The Cat Reminds the Rat of their Friendship

body.p:
What is stopping you
from approaching me, so that I can reward you for the good you’ve done by me Come to me, then, and don’t sever my brotherly ties;

p.n: If One Gives Up a Friend One Loses Out

body.p:
for he who takes
a friend and then loses those brotherly ties will be prevented from reaping the fruits of brotherhood and will make despair those people who hold affection for him.

Your favor, to me,
is a favor that cannot be forgotten, and you are entitled to seek my reward for it-as well as that of my brothers and friends.

So fear nothing from me,
for you should know that what has been declared to you will be bestowed.’ He then swore fervently emphasizing
to the truth of his words.”

p.n: The Rat Distinguishes Hidden from Overt Enmity

body.p:
“The rat said: ‘Many a hidden enmity is, on the surface, a friendship, which is
